issue_context.title: The titlebar is visible when using vintage opacity with a HIGH DPI display
issue_context.body:
_discovered in the 1.12 bug bash on 9/28_


![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18356694/135273925-4fea4eb4-d3b0-40df-943d-f7988ead0d10.png)

regressed in #11180
comments: I could not for the life of me get a repro, but @carlos-zamora has one, so he gets the cookie. I'm guessing this has to do with the changes to `IslandWindow` / `NonClientIslandWindow` in #11180. I'd start there. I'm guessing the titlebar isn't getting scaled right for the DPI, or at least the MARGINS we're passing to `DwnExtendFrameIntoClientArea` aren't scaled right? hard to say.

Ok. I did a bit of digging. Found a few interesting notes:
- it doesn't happen when `initialPosition` is set to the non-high DPI monitor
- it seems to particularly occur when the window is dragged from a high DPI to a non-high DPI monitor

Looking for the code where we refresh the window size on that drag. Surprisingly, `NonClientIslandWindow::_UpdateFrameMargins` isn't called when that happens.

review_comments: I'm mostly shocked that WM_DPICHANGING and WM_DPICHANGED didn't fire.
